subject: Service commitments & credit thresholds - maintenance carveout request
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora@cloudbridge.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rahul Sharma <rahul@cloudbridge.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Service commitments: uptime baseline and monthly credit caps

Diego —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our procurement team asked me to follow up with a few concrete asks so we can move the contract forward. High level: CloudBridge is comfortable with Redwood as our inference runtime but we need clarity and a small set of exceptions for our batched/maintenance workflows.

Specifically:
- What is Redwood’s standard hosted SLA (uptime %) for production API endpoints?
- How do monthly service credits calculate (formula + cap)? We need a firm cap for budgeting purposes.
- Can we get an exception carved out for scheduled batched-inference maintenance windows (we run large model cache compactions monthly)?

Procurement would like a short note we can attach to the purchase order that calls out the uptime percent and a maximum monthly credit as a percentage of committed spend.

I’ve attached a short doc with our expected maintenance pattern (CloudBridge-SLA-ask.pdf).

Appreciate any details — our target for signature is May 10 so we’re trying to lock these items down quickly.

Best,
Nora
Nora Patel
Head of Cloud Platform
CloudBridge

Attachments: CloudBridge-SLA-ask.pdf (1 page — maintenance cadence table)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service commitments: uptime baseline and monthly credit caps

Nora — thanks for the clear note and the attached cadence. Looping in Laura (commercial) and Ben (legal touchpoint) so we can align internally.

Quick answers up front (we can formalize in an amendment):
- Standard hosted uptime: Redwood’s baseline for hosted single-tenant APIs is 99.95% monthly availability (calculated on regional endpoint). We publish monthly uptime measurements and provide automated credit calculations.
- Credit formula: credits are prorated against monthly invoice for the affected service and triggered when availability drops below the stated threshold for that month. Separate buckets for availability vs. latency breaches.
- Typical cap: our default monthly cap is 30% of the monthly committed spend for the affected product. That cap is negotiable for enterprise deals.

Regarding your batched maintenance: we can offer a carveout for scheduled maintenance related to cache compaction/rebalancing if the windows are pre-notified and limited to a reasonable cadence. Our standard carveout language excludes maintenance events >

What I’d propose as a starting point for discussion:
- Maintain baseline 99.95% availability.
- Offer a carveout for up to 6 hours/month of scheduled batched maintenance (pre-scheduled, with at least 72h notice). Events beyond that reduce availability for the month and may trigger credits.
- Reduce the default monthly credit cap to 25% of committed spend for this agreement (we can go lower with multi-region commitments).

If that looks promising, Ben will draft a short SLA amendment and I’ll route it to your procurement. Also happy to run a 2-week pilot where we measure your maintenance pattern against our monitoring so we can calibrate how often the carveout would apply.

Can you confirm the monthly committed spend range (ballpark) so we can size the cap?

Thanks,

Diego Fernandez
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
Diego: +1 (415) 555-0176

From: Nora Patel <nora@cloudbridge.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rahul Sharma <rahul@cloudbridge.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service commitments: uptime baseline and monthly credit caps

Diego — thanks for the quick reply and for the suggested compromises. A few clarifications from procurement and finance:

- Our finance team wants a fixed, conservative cap for monthly credits to avoid runaway refunds. Ideally 20% of committed spend or less. Is that reachable if we sign a 12–18 month commit?
- The maintenance carveout is helpful; we run two scheduled compaction windows per month that can each be up to 3 hours. We can provide a monthly calendar and commit to 72h notice. Would Redwood accept a 6-hour allowance specifically for "batched maintenance (cache compaction / KV rebalance)" and exclude it from availability calculations?
- We reviewed 99.95% vs. 99.9% — given the distributed nature of our workload and the business impact, finance prefers to ask for 99.9% in the contract and accept credits for anything below that. Is there flexibility to set a lower baseline if it reduces credit exposure?

One additional ask: because we’re migrating a sizable batch job in month one, we’d like a one-time credit (pro-rated) should the migration cause service degradation during the first 30 days. Not a large ask — just to share risk.

Rahul (procurement) is on copy to coordinate paperwork. We’re signing up to $120k/mo committed spend in the first year; that should help you size the cap.

Thanks — Nora

Attachments: none

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora@cloudbridge.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service commitments: uptime baseline and monthly credit caps

Nora / Diego —

Thanks for the details. I’m Ben from commercial contracts — quick follow up with a compromise that should be straightforward for both teams: 

Proposal (draft amendment we can sign)
- Availability baseline: 99.93% monthly (compromise between 99.95% and 99.9%).
- Monthly credit cap: 20% of the monthly committed spend (applies across availability + latency credit buckets).
- Maintenance carveout: Up to 6 hours/month for scheduled batched maintenance (cache compaction / KV rebalance) excluded from availability calculation if pre-notified >=72h and scheduled in the agreed monthly window. Any ad-hoc unplanned maintenance counts toward availability.
- Migration protection: One-time pro-rated credit (capped at 5% of first month’s committed spend) for service impact directly attributable to the migration, conditional on advance notices and coordination with Redwood’s migration plan.

I’ve attached a short amendment draft (SLA-Amendment-draft.docx) that codifies the language above. If you confirm we’ll send to your procurement and legal for redline.

Next steps:
1) Nora / Rahul — confirm that 20% cap and 99.93% baseline are acceptable given $120k/mo commit.
2) If accepted, we’ll route the amendment and push for signature within 5 business days.
3) Optionally run the 2-week pilot to validate maintenance carveout frequency.

Happy to hop on a call if any of this needs live discussion.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Contracts Manager — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0241
